A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic reversal experiments, architectural comparisons, arithmetic-reasoning evaluations and error analyses in Sections 2–4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports a memory-layer control and repeated-seed JEPA results in Appendix B, Table 2.

M1.justification: The proposed concept-level prediction, JEPA with in-batch InfoNCE, memory-layer recognition and parametric forward-chaining procedures are retained. The expanded encoder/predictor explanation documents the existing architecture; the additional memory-layer control does not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic concept-level and surface-name reversal tasks, single-step arithmetic deductions and three-hop arithmetic search problems. The multiplicity conditions and branching factors remain unchanged. No new dataset, domain or task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The arithmetic comparison replaces Gemini-2.0-Flash-Thinking with Gemini-2.5-Pro, retaining o3-Mini-High and the standard transformer (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 5). Section 3.3 also newly reports evaluating a standard surface-prediction transformer equipped with memory layers.

E3.justification: v2 extends the control design by testing memory layers while retaining standard surface-level prediction. Existing data splits, model-size grids, checkpoint selection and arithmetic evaluation sample counts remain unchanged. Appendix A's training settings are identical; the added random-seed repetitions are assessed under E5.

E4.justification: v2 reports a memory-layer-only control testing whether mitigating entanglement suffices, adds initialization-stability analysis and updates the Gemini error analysis. It removes v1's brief reported checks concerning positional encodings and false-negative removal. The main depth, multiplicity and width analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 explicitly reports two additional random seeds, giving three runs for all nine JEPA depth configurations, and supplies means and standard deviations in Appendix B, Table 2. This introduces systematic replication and quantified uncertainty for a central experiment.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds three-run aggregate results, and Section 3.3 adds the memory-layer control's failure finding. The replacement Gemini model scores 0.90/0.75/0.55/0.35 across branching factors 10/20/30/40, versus 0.45/0.45/0.35/0.25 for the earlier comparator. Its error counts change from 6/3/1 to 7/2/1 for guesses/hallucinations/copy errors. Table 1, the original JEPA heatmaps and the proposed model's arithmetic scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The reversal and multiplicity definitions and Section 3.2's gradient-mixing derivation retain the same assumptions and mathematical content. The relocated explanation of depth-dependent entanglement and expanded JEPA discussion add no formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract shifts emphasis from arithmetic reasoning to systematic conceptual binding, but both contributions already appear in v1 and remain in v2. The principal claims about abstract reversal, conceptual inconsistency and entanglement, JEPA and memory layers, and arithmetic reasoning retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the added control as showing that memory layers help only after conceptual inconsistency is resolved, and interprets Table 2 as supporting stability across initialization. The main limitations concerning human scaffolding, known concept locations and synonymy remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the detailed recognition/verbalization control description and the manual-testing explanation associated with the former Gemini baseline. It adds reproducibility pointers and a prospective code-release statement alongside the retained code/data URL. Appendix A's hyperparameters, software and hardware disclosures are unchanged; actual resource availability changes are not established.

R1.justification: v2 removes the controlled-transformer-studies paragraph and associated citations, including Elhage et al., Prystawski et al. and Wang et al. It also removes the geometry-related future-work discussion citing Park and Jin. The central positioning relative to reversal-curse research, binding and JEPA remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted revisions to the abstract, introduction, experimental explanations and conclusion, and expands Appendix B's encoder/predictor explanation. Ethics and reproducibility statements and an LLM-writing-assistance appendix are added. The main section sequence and most substantive prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The JEPA schematic moves from v1 Appendix B, Figure 5, to v2 main-text Figure 2. v2 adds stability Table 2, expands Table 1's caption and updates the arithmetic plot's Gemini legend. Conference typography and float placement change, while the other diagrams and heatmap displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The three-seed results and additional memory-layer control strengthen support for the central depth and inconsistency arguments. Bringing the JEPA schematic into the main text and clarifying its components improve accessibility. These gains outweigh the limited loss of preliminary robustness checks and related-work context, while the unchanged synthetic task coverage and scaffolding limitations keep the overall improvement modest.
